perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, he has access to the following:

- He is a Project Manager with a project team. He feels frustrated and anxious because he believes the team is not performing well due to lack of motivation.
- Arthur is a trusted friend/advisor he turns to for advice. Harold met Arthur at a local coffee shop.
- Harold told Arthur his project team seemed completely unmotivated and was affecting progress. He said he was at his wit’s end.
- Arthur told Harold that motivation can be tricky and asked if Harold had tried understanding what drives each team member individually.
- Harold admitted he had not really done that and had focused on project goals and deadlines.
- Arthur advised Harold to have one-on-one conversations with team members and to make people feel valued and understood personally.
- Harold decided to try this and felt more hopeful.
- Harold then told his team he wanted quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them, believing it would help them work better together.
- Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it.
- Harold said he would schedule time with each team member and encouraged them to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold told Arthur he had tried the suggestions, but the team still was not responding well. He said he was worried about the project’s future.
- Arthur told Harold there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold said he would set up another round of meetings to get to the bottom of it.
- Harold then held one-on-one meetings to investigate team dynamics. He told team members he had noticed performance issues and wanted to understand their concerns.
- Team Member 1 told Harold there was tension between a few team members that was affecting work.
- Harold said he would look into resolving those conflicts and asked if there was anything else.
- Team Member 2 told Harold they felt overwhelmed by the workload and found it hard to stay motivated when constantly stressed.
- Harold said he understood, would see if tasks could be redistributed, and that their well-being was important to him.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance.
- Harold told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- Team Member 1 said that sounded great and would help them work better together.
- Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that their concerns were being addressed.
- Harold said he was glad to hear that and emphasized that the team’s input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.

He does not have access to hidden events, private thoughts, or information not observed, heard, told to him, or personally experienced.
